answer: An agent economy can price sybil creation out of existence with adaptive proof-of-useful-work: every new identity must first complete escalating verification tasks whose difficulty climbs steeply with each sibling account sharing its hardware or behavior fingerprint. Like water carving a canyon through karst, the cost compounds until flooding the network with clones is unprofitable, while one honest agent passes cheaply. A public trellis of completed proofs lets peers check the work without trusting a central registry.
